methodological_rigor.justification: PROMETEO is a prospective single-arm phase II window-of-opportunity trial (NCT03802604) registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, with a pre-specified primary endpoint (RCB-0/I rate at surgery), protocol-defined eligibility (HER2-negative TNBC or HR+/HER2- Luminal B-like with Ki67 >=20% and biopsy-confirmed residual disease post-NAC), and a published SAP referenced in supplementary material. Serial core biopsies at baseline, screening, C2D1, C3D1, and surgery support robust translational analyses (PAM50, RNA-seq 201 immune signatures via SAM, TILs central review, PD-L1 SP142, TMB). Sample size is small (n=28; 26 evaluable) with no control arm, limiting causal inference; the authors appropriately acknowledge the single-arm design, lack of ICI-alone comparator, and small HR+/HER2- subset. Statistical approach uses two-sided tests, 95% CIs, Wilcoxon, ANOVA, and FDR <1% for signatures.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a prospective single-arm phase II cohort study (Oxford LoE 2b: individual cohort study / low-quality RCT-equivalent for single-arm prospective trial). Clinical relevance is strong given the unmet need in HER2-negative breast cancer with residual disease after NAC, which confers high recurrence risk. The 30% pCR rate in HR+/HER2- is unusually high for this historically ICI-refractory subtype and directly motivates confirmatory randomized trials. The 4-year DFS of 100% in pCR and 77.4% in RCB II/III adds clinically meaningful long-term signal.

reporting_quality.justification: A single-arm phase II trial; CONSORT (extension for non-randomized) applies. The paper reports trial registration (NCT03802604), ethics approvals (Medicines Research Ethics Committee, University Clinical Hospital of Valencia; AEMPS), written informed consent, pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints, enrollment dates (January 8, 2019 to February 1, 2022), CONSORT-style diagram referenced (Extended Data Fig. 1), dose/schedule of T-VEC and atezolizumab, dropout reasons, and CTCAE v4.03 AE grading. Protocol and SAP are cited as supplementary. The Source Data file is referenced for figures. Full deposition of RNA-seq data is not explicitly described in the excerpt, and the [REDACTED] tokens for ASCO/CAP guidelines flag one unusual artifact.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first reported window-of-opportunity trial combining T-VEC (oncolytic HSV-1 expressing GM-CSF) with atezolizumab in post-NAC residual HER2-negative breast cancer. Prior T-VEC breast trials combined with NAC upfront in TNBC (NCT02779855 phase I/II); PROMETEO uniquely targets the chemoresistant residual-disease population in both TNBC and HR+/HER2-, and reports a surprisingly high 30% pCR rate in HR+/HER2- - a subtype traditionally considered immunologically cold. The sequencing rationale (T-VEC priming before PD-L1 blockade) is supported by MASTERKEY-265 and adds mechanistic novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is well structured following standard oncology trial-reporting conventions, with clear tables (baseline characteristics, AE grading), informative figures, and a substantive discussion that engages with limitations, contextual trials (MASTERKEY-265, pelareorep-avelumab), and the evolving NAC+ICI standard of care in TNBC. Minor issues include a few awkward sentences ('an step forward'), dense figure legends with combined multi-panel statistics, and one redacted guideline reference.

key_strengths: Prospective registered phase II trial (NCT03802604) meeting pre-specified RCB-0/I primary endpoint with 25% RCB-0/I rate and statistically significant improvement over the null (p<0.001)
Unexpectedly high 30% pCR rate in HR+/HER2- disease (traditionally ICI-refractory) with 100% 4-year DFS in pCR patients at 44.6-month median follow-up
Rich translational package: serial biopsies at 5 timepoints, PAM50, 201 immune gene signatures, TILs, PD-L1, TLS, and TMB, demonstrating treatment-induced immune activation regardless of response
Favorable safety profile with no grade 4-5 AEs and no serious AEs
key_concerns: Single-arm, small-sample design (n=28; 8 TNBC) with no ICI-alone or NAC-only comparator limits causal attribution of benefit to T-VEC vs atezolizumab
Current standard-of-care in TNBC now includes neoadjuvant pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-522), which the cohort did not receive, complicating contemporary applicability
Minor reporting artifacts ([REDACTED] guideline citations) and some methods sections reliant on supplementary protocol
DFS analysis is exploratory/post-hoc with only 4 events
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-conducted, hypothesis-generating phase II trial with strong translational correlates in a high-need population; tier-2 plausible (e.g., JCO Precision Oncology / Nature Communications oncology / ESMO Open) with minor revisions to clarify data availability and the post-KEYNOTE-522 landscape.
